stage: G6 bounded linear VRAM float vertex spans
scope: Exact CPU vertex preparation optimization, not native FPS or completed benchmark acceptance.
change: Dense FLOAT1..4 attributes backed by linear VRAM share one checked, copied source span, at most 4 MiB and four times the indexed attribute payload.
Direct DWORD loads preserve all IEEE float payload bits and missing-component defaults; no float conversion or persistent guest data cache.
Paged/system-memory DMA, zero stride and sparse spans retain the original per-vertex path.
regression: Pre-change implementation fails the new one-span check (4 reads versus 1).
48 combinations of FLOAT1..4, overlapping/unaligned strides, signed base vertex, duplicates, raw NaN/negative-zero/infinity payloads.
Inclusive limit/read permission rejection preserves source bytes.
Legal paged and physical-memory draws skip an inaccessible intermediate page; reading the bounding span is explicitly shown to fail.
State/graph/texture/DMA suites, entire real WebGPU render suite, Closure 0 errors/warnings.

microbenchmark.gc: Explicit GC before each measured round, outside CPU/wall counters.
microbenchmark.interpretation: Indexed float/color/current workload improves 54.29 to 32.19 ms. Unchanged index controls vary by about 12-15%; unchanged inline control is 32.49/32.30 ms. Concurrent microbenchmarks are not native performance gates.
